newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at three-month high vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at three-month high vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at a new three-month high of 8.2922 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Thursday, from Wednesday's 8.2924, due to China's surging foreign trade surplus, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2925.
Beijing said on Tuesday that China's foreign trade surplus was $10.29 billion in the first four months of this year, against a deficit of $607 million for the same period in 1996.
The yuan was also boosted on Thursday by recent local media reports that more of the approved foreign banks had started to do local currency business, traders said.

The yuan opened up at 8.2922 and rose steadily early in the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2912 before falling to hit a low of 8.2924. Trading was active with most business done at 8.2920, traders said.
One dealer said some profit-taking knocked the yuan off its high but did not hurt pro-yuan market sentiment.
"Pro-yuan sentiment has been strengthening again after the foreign trade data was announced," he said.
A second dealer said recent positive factors were likely to push the yuan further up in the short term. "Most people think the yuan has potential for further rises," he said.
Traders said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2920 level on Friday.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 7.1464 from 6.9740 against 100 Japanese yen and down slightly at the day's lowest of 1.0724 from 1.0722 against the Hong Kong dollar.
